incidents.victim: Government officials, military, journalists & activists (US, Europe, Ukraine)
incidents.vector: Phishing messages impersonating Signal/WhatsApp/Telegram support staff trick high-value targets into surrendering verification codes, PINs and backup recovery keys.
incidents.impact: FBI, CISA and Ukraine's SBU warn of an ongoing campaign hijacking secure-messaging accounts of high-intelligence-value individuals; attackers can read historical and group messages and persist even after account re-creation on the same number.

incidents.vector: Russia's long-running espionage group expanded its toolkit with new custom malware (tracked as 'StockStay') deployed against Ukrainian targets.
incidents.impact: Continued cyber-espionage operations against Ukraine aimed at intelligence collection, with newly observed malware broadening the group's access and persistence.

incidents.victim: Southeast Asian governments and state-owned energy infrastructure
incidents.vector: ASPX web shells dropped via exploited web apps, followed by open-source tunneling tools (SoftEther VPN, VNT) and a new bespoke backdoor ('TinyRCT') for command execution, screen capture and data theft.
incidents.impact: Chinese-speaking actors compromised multiple government entities and at least two state-owned critical energy infrastructure operators across a Southeast Asian country, exfiltrating databases and web-server source code.

incidents.victim: Hospitality and hotel industry (Europe and Asia)
incidents.vector: Photo-themed ZIP archives with fake image shortcut (.lnk) files launch obfuscated PowerShell and a Node.js implant; phishing emails abuse Calendly and Google redirects to pass SPF/DKIM/DMARC checks ('authentication laundering').
incidents.impact: Multi-stage intrusions against hotel front-desk and reservations staff established dual registry persistence and C2 beaconing since April 2026; Microsoft assesses the actor is staging victims for follow-on activity.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-20230, an unauthenticated SSRF in the CUCM WebDialer service chained to write JSP web shells and escalate to root, weaponized within 24 hours of a public proof-of-concept.
incidents.impact: Attackers gained root on internet-exposed CUCM systems used across healthcare, finance and government; organizations with WebDialer enabled and unpatched should assume they were scanned or compromised.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Check Point Remote Access VPN
incidents.vector: Qilin ransomware affiliate exploited CVE-2026-50751, a CVSS 9.3 authentication-bypass in Check Point VPN (IKEv1), to establish fully authenticated sessions with no valid password, then used Rclone and Tox-based C2 for exfiltration.
incidents.impact: Dozens of organizations worldwide were breached starting in early May — roughly six weeks before the June 21 CISA directive — leaving already-compromised victims with an attacker operating as a trusted user.

incidents.vector: Attack on the operator's IT systems; a pro-Russian group ('IT Army of Russia') claimed it had breached infrastructure weeks earlier and exfiltrated a user database.
incidents.impact: Ukrposhta's mobile application suffered temporary outages following an overnight attack on its IT systems; the operator did not confirm data theft.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack on the company's IT systems disrupting logistics and accounting functions; a separate regional state dairy site was defaced with fake contamination claims.
incidents.impact: The dairy was forced to process shipments and paperwork manually; production continued but document and shipment handling slowed, the latest in a string of attacks on Russia's dairy sector.

incidents.victim: Organizations using Fortinet, Sophos and MSSQL services (global)
incidents.vector: Internet-wide password spraying and exploitation of old Fortinet vulnerabilities, plus a custom 'FortigateSniffer' script that intercepts credentials across 24 protocols passing through firewalls; harvested hashes are GPU-cracked and validated inside victim networks.
incidents.impact: The 'FortiBleed' campaign by a Russian-speaking access broker harvested credentials far beyond the 74,000 leaked Fortinet passwords found online; network access is being sold to other groups and the operation remains active.

incidents.vector: Rogue peering connections and stolen certificate material gave SSH access, then zero-day CVE-2026-20245 in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager was exploited via a malicious CSV upload to gain root and create a hidden 'troot' account.
incidents.impact: A state-sponsored actor achieved root on a service provider's SD-WAN orchestration plane, exfiltrated fabric configurations and used extensive anti-forensic cleanup to evade detection — a foothold enabling wide-scale access to internal enterprise traffic.

incidents.vector: Data-theft and extortion; the 'World Leaks' group listed the company and claims to have stolen more than 200,000 documents.
incidents.impact: Tata Electronics confirmed a security breach after the group claimed theft of sensitive documents, allegedly including data on Apple and Tesla electronic components.

incidents.vector: Data taken from a third-party company that managed the agency's mobile device management (MDM) platform; the breach is linked to a wave of attacks on Ivanti EPMM servers.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole names, phone numbers and email addresses of Belgian intelligence service officials — a sensitive exposure of personnel running counter-intelligence operations.

incidents.victim: Transport for London, M&S, Co-op, Harrods, US healthcare providers
incidents.vector: SIM-swapping, voice/SMS phishing and social engineering to steal employee credentials and single sign-on access, used for network intrusions and ransom attacks.
incidents.impact: Two key 'Scattered Spider' members pleaded guilty in the UK over the August 2024 Transport for London attack and related intrusions; a US indictment ties the group to 120 intrusions across 47 entities and at least $115M in ransom payments.

incidents.victim: Klue and its corporate customers (LastPass, Snyk, security firms)
incidents.vector: A compromised legacy credential for an integration service let attackers steal OAuth tokens that customers used to connect Klue to Salesforce, then download data from those Salesforce accounts.
incidents.impact: At least eight companies — including LastPass and several cybersecurity firms — had Salesforce data stolen via the Klue supply-chain breach; a group calling itself 'Icarus' is extorting victims and leaking data.

incidents.victim: North American medical, academic, and military research institutions
incidents.vector: Compromise of externally facing REDCap research servers, deployment of custom 'INFINITERED' malware to harvest credentials, then abuse of enterprise email compliance rules to covertly BCC-forward matched messages for exfiltration.
incidents.impact: A PRC-nexus actor (UNC6508) remained undetected since 2023 inside research organizations, pursuing AI, defense, uncrewed-systems and medical research; Google disrupted the infrastructure and notified victims.

incidents.victim: Iranian banks (Bank Melli, Tejarat, Saderat, Export Development Bank)
incidents.vector: Attack reportedly targeted shared communications infrastructure used by the four banks, knocking out online portals and mobile apps.
incidents.impact: Online banking and mobile apps for four of Iran's largest banks were disrupted over a weekend; intelligence sources believe Israeli hackers were likely responsible. The banking council said no customer data was accessed.
